What we do?

We develop digital therapeutics to address unmet medical needs in hematology and oncology. 

How it works?

First we build networks of doctors and patients designed to track, predict and prevent disease. Second, we validate the safety and efficacy of our interventions in pivotal clinical studies to obtain regulatory clearance (SaMD). Finally, we aim to commercialize our products as prescription digital therapeutics (DTx).

Where are we now?

Today, we are the standard in digital hematology:

* Our hemophilia network covers 33% of all patients and providers in the US. 
* We bested 20+ competitors, including several Fortune 500 companies. 
* Our clients include: Sanofi, Bayer, Novo Nordisk, Biogen, and Roche.
long_description.after:

* Singular network architecture and data capturing capabilities help identify patients with unmet needs in real-time; unlocking opportunities to improve health outcomes and additional revenue for pharma

* Microhealth has achieved product-market fit in the hemophilia and rare blood disorders space

Today, we are the world's leader in digital hematology:

long_description.before:
With Ancana, you can own a 1/4 or 1/8 share of the home and split expenses with the other co-owners. If you buy a 1/4 share of a home, you have access to it for 3 months of the year. For each property we set up the investment trust, find qualified co-owners, and handle the entire real estate purchase transaction. Costs are split amongst the co-owners, and we take care of the furnishing and ongoing property management.

We accomplish this by creating an investment trust for each property and dividing it into individual, purchasable shares that represent ownership in the property. We furnish each home and find and vet the co-owners. Once all of the shares of the property are sold, we retain no ownership stake in the property and transition into the role of property manager, ensuring the home is well maintained and handling any issues that arise. Unlike a timeshare, Ancana owners own a real asset (the property) versus a block of time. If you decide you want to sell your share, you are free to do so at any time, either through us or on the open market, and capture any appreciation the property has accrued.
long_description.after: Ancana is a marketplace for fully managed, co-owned vacation homes. Owners buy a real share of a property alongside a small group of vetted co-owners, each with guaranteed usage time every year. Unused weeks can be rented out or swapped for stays at other Ancana properties, so the ownership stays useful even as plans change. Ancana handles everything behind the purchase — setting up the ownership structure, vetting and matching co-owners, and managing the transaction — then runs the property year-round, from furnishing to bookings and maintenance. We operate in Mexico, the US, and Spain, each with different legal and regulatory requirements for ownership, and solving that structuring problem market by market is what makes the model hold up as we expand.

one_liner.before: Marketplace to buy managed vacation homes through fractional ownership
one_liner.after: Marketplace for vacation home co-ownership, fully managed

long_description.before: Adentris is an AI compliance copilot for hospitals and clinics. We are like Grammarly for doctors, finding and fixing mistakes that lead to denied insurance claims or patient lawsuits. The industry today spends $40B doing this manually.
long_description.after: US healthcare providers lose billions every year to denied claims, most of them traced back to documentation and coding gaps no one catches until the payer says no. Adentris is an AI revenue integrity platform that catches them first. Our AI agents read EHR and payer interfaces directly, no API integration required, across five modules: documentation, coding QA, prior authorization, appeals and denials, and discharge summaries. And for providers that don't have their own CDI or billing teams, we run billing as a service on top of the platform.

long_description.before:
Skillsync lets you push your agents' sessions the way you push code. Everything lands in one searchable place. The best sessions become skills any agent can load. Works across your team!

Today, all that thinking, what worked, what didn't, and why, is scattered across Claude Code, Codex, Hermes, whatever each engineer prefers. It vanishes when the session closes. Skillsync captures it, so every agent builds like your best engineer. The more your team ships, the smarter your agents get. Engineering culture stops being tribal knowledge. It becomes explicit, shared, and reusable.
long_description.after:
Skillsync is a local-first desktop app that frees your context from any single coding agent. Move a full session, including the conversation, reasoning, and tool history, between Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and any other agent with nothing lost. Keep your skills and memory in one searchable place, accessible from any agent via MCP. And when your team perfects a skill, it syncs to everyone automatically, so you stop digging through Slack threads and zip files to find the version that actually works.

The engine that translates sessions across agent formats, txcript, is open source and written in Rust. Say it once, and every agent and teammate has it.

Turnstone is the AI workspace where your agents already know you. Connect your apps (e.g. email, calendar, Slack, Drive) and your local folders. Turnstone turns all of it into your second brain and continuously updates it.

Spin up agents (e.g. chief of staff, research, GTM) that all share that brain, so you stop re-explaining yourself and start getting real work done.

It all lives on your machine and runs on any model you already pay for. Ask your agent once, and it's done.

one_liner.after: Work with agents that already know you

long_description.before:
Prized lets non-engineers build, deploy, and share secure internal tools with AI, no engineering required. You don't need to know where the data lives, what APIs to use, or which connectors you need. Just describe what you want (a customer lookup, a dashboard, an approval flow), and Prized builds the tool on top of the right company data inside a governed boundary.

The people who feel the pain of missing internal tools most are non-engineers. They understand the workflow best but are blocked by the software layer, so they wait on engineering, duct-tape spreadsheets together, or increasingly rip company data into Claude Code and Cursor with no thought to permissions, sharing, or governance.

Prized makes security the default, enforced in the infrastructure rather than left to whoever built the tool. Each tool gets access only to the tables and integrations it was explicitly granted, credentials are workspace-scoped so tools can't cross org boundaries, and outbound calls go through a controlled layer. 

As an employee builds and shares, a teammate forks it and re-points it at their own data, and over time the company builds up a library of governed tools it actually owns.

Hudson was founding engineer at Gander (F24, acquired by Archer), then full-stack at Suno. Marinos studied CS and ME at Stanford and was on the same Gander team.
long_description.after:
Prized is a cloud development environment that feels local on your Mac. 

Developers get a dedicated, persistent machine with their repos, dependencies, and tools already configured. 

Files sync into a real local folder, remote ports appear on localhost, and terminals persist through tmux, so developers and coding agents can keep working even after the laptop closes. 

Machines can be resized or cloned as workloads grow, without rebuilding the development environment.

one_liner.after: A cloud devbox that feels local
